title: FAST Security with a Revealed S-Box-Generation Key
summary: FAST has a known-S security model, but it remains open whether comparable security can be proved when the S-box-generation key is revealed and the S-box pool is generated from a random key.

formal_statement.body: For FAST, whose known-$S$ security model is formalized as $\mathsf{IND}_{K_S}^{\mathsf{sprp}}$ security, determine whether security can be established when the S-box-generation key $K_S$ is revealed to the adversary while the S-box pool $S$ is still generated by PRNG2 from a random $K_S$ in the security game. The unresolved task is to analyze this revealed-$K_S$ model using the same security parameters $(T,q,\varepsilon)$ and to determine whether a corresponding security argument or reduction can be proved.

scope.domain: Provable security for FAST under disclosure of its S-box-generation key.
assumptions: The security game reveals the S-box-generation key to the adversary while generating the S-box pool with PRNG2 from a random such key.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether FAST is secure in this revealed-key game and whether a corresponding security argument or reduction can be proved.

citations.label: FAST: Secure and High Performance Format-Preserving Encryption and Tokenization

progress.summary: After defining the known-S security model, the paper proposes revealing the S-box-generation key while generating the S-box pool from a random key. It leaves the corresponding security argument as a possible extension.
citation_labels: F. Betül Durak et al., FAST: Secure and High Performance Format-Preserving Encryption and Tokenization
